data.narrative:
Atom Bodies is a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Tyler Hayes, Doug Satzger, and Eric Monsef, having raised $142.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private comparables including Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, and Recursion Pharmaceuticals.

Of three valuation methods evaluated, only Stage-Progression proved applicable. This method uses the company's $142.2M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression to the next financing stage, yielding $284M. Peer-Median anchoring was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage private peers meeting minimum data thresholds (need ≥3; identified 0 in narrow filters). Public-Comp Anchoring also could not be applied because Atom Bodies' revenue is not disclosed, preventing use of the public sector's 8.1x median P/S multiple.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $242M to $327M, centered on $284M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the Stage-Progression point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue-based anchoring (which would enable public-comp triangulation) and limited private-peer visibility at this specific stage and sector positioning. The single-method foundation suggests this valuation should be stress-tested against forward revenue projections and comparable financing rounds once additional data materiality permits secondary method validation.
